papers.title_in_file: Photonic Nonlinearities via Quantum Zeno Blockade
papers.version_note: arXiv:1303.5666v1 (22 Mar 2013), Letter plus supplementary material (pages 6 and 7 of the text layer).
papers.what_it_is: A theory and simulation Letter proposing a deterministic single-photon phase gate from quantum Zeno blockade in a lithium-niobate microdisk resonator with sum-frequency generation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for a lithium-niobate microresonator, a deterministic phase gate can be realized between single photons with near-unity fidelity.
quotes: we ﬁnd that a deterministic phase gate can be realized between single photons with near-unity ﬁdelity
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulation result with parameters the authors chose; no experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is a numerical simulation, not a device measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that, once the multimode nature of light propagation in a Kerr medium is taken into account, no useful cross-phase modulation effect can be produced in such systems even with an unrealistically giant Kerr nonlinearity (cited to refs 16 and 17).
quotes: it was recently discovered that no useful XPM eﬀect can be produced in such systems even with an unrealistically giant Kerr nonlinearity [16, 17]
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work (Shapiro 2006; Gea-Banacloche 2010).

assertions.value: The authors state that the fundamental reason is that causality prohibits a non-negligible cross-phase modulation phase shift without significant quantum noise.
quotes: The fundamental reason turns out to be that causality prohibits XPM phase shift of any non-negligible amount without signiﬁcant quantum noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to earlier work in the same paragraph; not derived here.

assertions.value: The authors state that the intuition that a weak Kerr nonlinearity can give a single-photon cross-phase shift, if the nonlinearity is giant enough, rests on an incorrect single-mode argument.
quotes: This logic, unfortunately, is based on an incorrect single-mode argument.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated by the authors, supported by citation to refs 16 and 17.

assertions.value: The authors describe quantum Zeno blockade as occurring when a quantum system interacts with external degrees of freedom through a nonlinear channel, so that with strong nonlinear coupling a single photon in a mode can block (suppress) additional photons from coupling into that mode.
quotes: which occurs when a quantum system interacts with external degrees of freedom through a nonlinear channel
occupation of a certain quantum mode by a single photon can “block” (more precisely, suppress) additional photons from coupling into that mode [18, 19]
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own working definition of quantum Zeno blockade, Introduction p.1.

assertions.value: The authors set up the gate as a lithium-niobate microdisk cavity evanescently coupled to a prism, with the cavity designed to be in resonance with both the pump (control) and the signal (target).
quotes: It consists of a LN microdisk cavity evanescently coupled to a prism.
The cavity is designed to be in resonance with both the pump (control) and the signal (target).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own gate setup, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the chi-2 nonlinearity of lithium niobate can lead to intracavity sum-frequency or difference-frequency generation between signal and pump, and that only sum-frequency generation is considered as a specific example.
quotes: The χ(2) nonlinearity of LN can lead to intracavity sum-frequency generation (SFG) or diﬀerencefrequency generation (DFG) between the signal and the pump.
Only SFG is considered in the following as a speciﬁc example.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper limits its analysis to sum-frequency generation, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that with the pump off the signal field couples into the disk through the prism and then exits with a pi phase shift relative to its input.
quotes: Through the prism, the signal ﬁeld evanescently couples into the disk and then exits with a π phase shift relative to its input.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's description of the pump-off gate operation, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in either the CQZ or the IQZ regime, with the pump on the signal's coupling into the disk is suppressed and the signal reflects (exits) with its phase unchanged.
quotes: In either the CQZ or the IQZ regime, the signal’s coupling into disk is thus suppressed and it reﬂects (exits) with its phase unchanged.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's description of the pump-on gate operation, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors define the coherent quantum Zeno (CQZ) regime as the case where the cavity is resonant for the sum-frequency field with high intrinsic quality factor; coherent sum-frequency generation then acts as a continuous measurement that shifts the disk away from resonance with the signal, preventing the signal photon from entering the cavity.
quotes: In the CQZ case, the cavity is resonant for the SF ﬁeld with high intrinsic quality factor
Coherent SFG process thus works as a continuous measurement, which shifts the disk away from resonance with the signal, preventing the signal photon from entering the cavity.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the CQZ regime, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors define the incoherent quantum Zeno (IQZ) regime as the case with a short-lived cavity sum-frequency field, which together with the high potential for sum-frequency generation opens a strong dissipation channel for the intracavity signal field, destroying the cavity resonance and preventing the signal photon from entering.
quotes: In the IQZ case, a short-lived cavity SF ﬁeld, together with the high potential for SFG, opens a strong dissipation channel for the intracavity signal ﬁeld,
destroying the cavity resonance and preventing the signal photon from entering the cavity.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the IQZ regime, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that for a typical lithium-niobate microdisk with radius about 1.5 mm (as printed in the text layer) and intrinsic Q above the printed value 107, the resonance linewidth is much smaller than the free-spectral range, so only a single cavity mode is excited by each applied quasi-monochromatic field.
quotes: For a typical LN microdisk with radius R ≃ 1.5 mm and Qi > 107 [27], the resonance linewidth is much smaller than the cavity’s free-spectral range.
It is thus valid to consider only a single cavity mode being excited by the corresponding applied external quasimonochromatic ﬁeld.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' stated modeling scope, p.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the radius as 1.5 mm, while the later disks are tens of micrometres; the unit may be a text-layer or typesetting error, which this reader cannot settle from the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that a temporally multimode quantum description is needed to capture the behavior of pulsed optical signals, and use an effective real-space Hamiltonian (Eq. 1) with a cavity-coupling term and an intracavity sum-frequency generation term with nonlinear coupling coefficient Upsilon.
quotes: To capture the temporal behavior of pulsed optical signals, a temporally multimode quantum description is needed.
We consider an eﬀective real-space Hamiltonian speciﬁc to our gate system, as follows [28]:
The last two terms in Eq. (1) describe the intracavity SFG process, where Υ is the nonlinear coupling coeﬃcient.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its model, p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the group velocity is assumed the same for all pulsed fields, and that the equations neglect decay of the whispering-gallery modes because the coupling quality factor is taken much smaller than the intrinsic quality factor.
quotes: vg is the group velocity which is assumed to be the same for all the pulsed ﬁelds
In arriving at Eq. (1), we have assumed Qcµ ≪ Qiµ and thus have neglected terms that describe decay of the WGMs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Assumptions the authors state for their model, pp.2-3.

assertions.value: The authors report, from analytical whispering-gallery mode profiles, that the nonlinear coupling coefficient Upsilon reaches 140 and 337 MHz for disk radii of about 50 and 20 micrometres respectively; Fig. 2 is a least-squares fit of log10 Upsilon against log10 R.
assertions.anchor: Model section and Fig. 2, p.2 to p.3
quotes: In Fig. 2 we plot Υ as a function of R calculated using analytical WGM proﬁles
Υ = 140 and 337 MHz are shown to be obtained for R ≈ 50 and 20 µm, re-
assertions.certainty_reason: A calculated value that depends on the chosen mode combinations and quasi-phase-matching pattern.

assertions.value: The authors state that Upsilon values this large are potentially realizable because high-quality lithium-niobate microdisks with radius as small as 40 micrometres have been fabricated by manual polishing, and that even smaller disks are expected with automated machining and polishing.
quotes: because high-quality LN microdisks with R as small as
40 µm have been fabricated via manual polishing tech-
Even smaller disks are expected to be fabri-
assertions.certainty_reason: Rests on a private communication (ref 29); not verifiable from the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The fabrication claim cites a private communication, so it is not independently checkable.

assertions.value: The authors state that, with commercially available lithium-niobate crystals (absorption loss of about 10 to the minus 4 per cm, printed flat) the absorption limit on intrinsic Q is about 108 (exponent printed flat), and that ultralow-absorption doped crystals (printed 10−5 cm−1) would allow intrinsic Q near 109 (exponent printed flat).
quotes: absorption loss in commercially-available LN crystals is usually ∼ 10−4/cm or higher, which imposes a high limit of Qµi ∼ 108
ultralow absorption loss ( 10−5 cm−1, bounded by measurement precision) has
Using such crystals, microdisks with Qiµ 109 can be fabricated.
assertions.certainty_reason: Attributed to refs 32 and 33; the text layer lost a comparison sign.

assertions.value: The authors state that they take intrinsic quality factor 109 (exponent printed flat), for which mode decay can be ignored when the coupling quality factor is of order 108 (exponent printed flat; the relation sign was lost), and that this is set by the disk-prism distance.
quotes: Based upon the above analysis, we will take Qµi = 109, for which decay of the WGMs can be ignored when Qcµ 108.
can be realized by adjusting the distance between the disk and
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's stated simulation parameters, p.3.
assertions.reader_inference: The relation sign between the coupling Q and 108 was lost in the text layer.

assertions.value: The authors write the joint state of signal, pump and sum-frequency photons in its most general form and derive coupled partial differential equations (Eq. 2a to 2e) from the Schroedinger equation; the output two-photon state is decomposed into Schmidt modes with eigenvalues a_n ordered a1 > a2 > ...
quotes: Plugging the Hamiltonian of Eq. (1) and the quantum state |Ψ(t) into the Schr¨odinger equation, the following partial diﬀerential equations can be derived:
with eignvalues
which are ordered such that a1 > a2 > · · · ≥ 0.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own formulation of the model equations, p.3.

assertions.value: The authors state that a near-unity squared first Schmidt coefficient together with a large overlap between the first signal output mode and the input signal, quantified by the fidelity, signifies high-performance switching when the pump is on.
quotes: quantiﬁed by the ﬁdelity
then signify high-
performance switching when the pump is on.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own performance measures, p.3.

assertions.value: The authors report that with coupling quality factors of 108 (exponent printed flat), Upsilon of 610 MHz, and two 500 ns (FWHM) Gaussian signal and pump pulses separated by 60 ns, the output photons are in an entangled two-photon state with Schmidt coefficients a1 = 0.77, a2 = 0.52 and a3 = 0.25, and negligible higher coefficients.
assertions.anchor: Gate performance section, Fig. 3, p.3 to p.4
quotes: we ﬁrst consider Qsc,p,f = 108, Υ = 610 MHz, and two 500 ns (FWHM) Gaussian signal and pump pulses with a separation of 60 ns.
the output photons turn out to be in an entangled two-photon state with a1 = 0.77, a2 = 0.52, a3 = 0.25, and an>3 ≃ 0.
assertions.certainty_reason: A single numerical simulation at one parameter set.
assertions.reader_inference: With a1 = 0.77 the gate does not work as a clean phase gate for Gaussian pulses; the authors present it as entanglement generation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Gaussian-pulse result points to a viable approach for on-demand generation of entanglement using two initially uncorrelated photons.
quotes: This result points to a viable approach for on-demand generation of entanglement using two initially uncorrelated photons
assertions.certainty_reason: An application the authors suggest; not tested.

assertions.value: The authors explain that quantum Zeno blockade is effective only if the pump photon is in the cavity, so the signal phase switches only if the signal arrives within the cavity lifetime of the pump photon; with a cavity lifetime of about 100 ns, five times smaller than the pulse widths, the output signal is a superposition of phase changed and unchanged states and the two photons exit entangled.
assertions.anchor: Gate performance section, p.3 to p.4
quotes: it is because the QZB is eﬀective only if the pump photon is in the cavity.
the cavity lifetime is about 100 ns for both the signal and pump photons, which is ﬁve times smaller than their pulse widths.
the two photons therefore exit the cavity in an entangled state.
assertions.certainty_reason: A qualitative explanation supported by a toy model, not proved.

assertions.value: The authors state that in a toy model with pump and signal each in an equal superposition of two time modes, an ideal quantum Zeno blockade yields an output entangled state of the form (|t0>|t1+D> + |t1>|t0+D> - |t0>|t0+D> - |t1>|t1+D>)/2.
assertions.anchor: Gate performance section, toy model, p.4
quotes: This phenomenon can be intuitively understood by considering a toy model
will be in an entangled state of |t0 p|t1 + ∆ s + |t1 p|t0 + ∆ s − |t0 p|t0 + ∆ s − |t1 p|t1 + ∆ s /2.
assertions.certainty_reason: An intuitive toy model with the text layer's bra-ket symbols partly lost; no derivation given.

assertions.value: The authors propose using photons in exponentially rising pulses whose temporal shapes replicate the time-reversed cavity leakage modes, so that the entire pump pulse is in the cavity when the signal arrives and the signal's phase is switched with certainty.
quotes: we propose to use photons in exponentially rising pulses whose temporal shapes replicate the “time reversed” cavity leakage modes [25]
This allows the entire pulse of the pump photon to be in the cavity when the signal photon arrives, so that the latter’s phase is switched with certainty.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' design proposal, tested only by the simulation below.

assertions.value: The authors report, for the CQZ simulation with exponentially rising pulses (pump and sum-frequency coupling quality factors 108 and signal coupling quality factor 107, exponents printed flat, other parameters as in the Gaussian case), that with the pump on the first Schmidt eigenfunction matches the input pulse shape with fidelity 0.99 and the output signal photon occupies this eigenmode with probability 0.98.
assertions.anchor: Gate performance section, Fig. 4(b), p.4 to p.5
quotes: taking Qpc,f = 108, Qsc = 107, and assuming all other parameters to be the same as in the Gaussian-pulse case considered above.
This ﬁrst eigenfunction matches the input pulse shape very well and the ﬁdelity reaches 0.99.
The probability for the output signal photon to occupy this eigenmode is 0.98.
assertions.certainty_reason: A single numerical simulation at one parameter set; no experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The 0.99 fidelity and 0.98 probability are simulated values, not device measurements.

assertions.value: The authors report that with the pump off the signal output is phase shifted by pi and temporally reversed, indicating the photon coupled into the cavity and out; with the signal off the pump behaves the same way; and with the signal on the pump couples into the disk and exits as if the signal photon did not exist.
assertions.anchor: Gate performance section, Fig. 4(a), 4(c), 4(d), p.4 to p.5
quotes: Except for the π phase shift, the temporal proﬁle of the signal output is reversed indicating that the signal photon coupled into the cavity and then out.
The pulse evolution is similar to the signal’s in the pump-OFF case.
the pump photon couples into disk and then exits as if the signal
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results at one parameter set.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the pump-off and signal-off cases the pulses start to leak out only after they have been entirely coupled in.
quotes: Both Figs. 4(a) and 4(c) show that the pulses start to leak out only after they have been entirely coupled in.
assertions.certainty_reason: Read from a simulated plot.

assertions.value: The authors report that both the fidelity and the probability of occupying the first Schmidt eigenmode saturate as Upsilon increases, and state that for a disk radius smaller than 25 micrometres good single-photon switching performance can be expected.
quotes: Both plots show a saturation feature as Υ increases.
As long as the disk radius is smaller than 25 µm, good single-photon switching performance can be expected.
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulated sweep over Upsilon; the 25 micrometre threshold is the authors' reading of it.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the IQZ case, with sum-frequency intrinsic quality factor about 105 and signal and pump about 109 (exponents printed flat), the probability of occupying the first eigenmode is 0.9 but the fidelity with the input is only 0.51, and sum-frequency dissipation introduces more than 85% loss to the signal energy, so the switch is significantly worse than in the CQZ case.
assertions.anchor: Supplementary material, section III, Fig. 1, p.6 to p.7
quotes: a smaller Qif ∼ 105 while still retaining Qsi,p ∼ 109
Although the probability of occupying the ﬁrst eigenmode is 0.9, the ﬁdelity of the output with the input is only 0.51, and the dissipation at the SF introduces > 85% loss to the signal energy.
assertions.certainty_reason: A single simulation at one parameter set.

assertions.value: The authors state that the IQZ case performs worse because, with high loss for the cavity sum-frequency field, the efficiency of sum-frequency generation is significantly reduced by the quantum Zeno effect, so more of the signal pulse couples into the cavity and is lost through sum-frequency generation.
quotes: the eﬃciency for SFG is signiﬁcantly reduced owing to the quantum Zeno eﬀect. More of the signal pulse couples into the cavity, which sees loss through SFG and then leads to worse switching performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: A qualitative explanation by the authors, not separately tested.

assertions.value: The authors state that the nonlinear coupling coefficient depends on the quasi-phase-matching pattern and the overlap of the cavity field profiles, and that to maximize the overlap integral they use only fundamental modes with q = 1 and l = m, subject to energy conservation and a quasi-phase-matching condition.
assertions.anchor: Supplementary material, section II, Eqs. (2) to (4), p.6
quotes: Equation (2) shows that the feasible value for Υ depends on both the QPM pattern and the overlap of the cavity ﬁeld proﬁles.
we only consider the fundamental modes with q = 1 and l = m.
ωs + ωp = ωf , kj + ms + mp − mf = 0.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own method for computing Upsilon, supplementary section II.

assertions.value: The authors state that they numerically searched for combinations of signal, pump and sum-frequency modes within the near-infrared to telecom-band range, found 15 or more combinations for a given radius, and plotted the largest Upsilon in Fig. 2.
quotes: we numerically search for combinations of the cavity signal, pump, and SF modes within the near-infrared to the telecom-band range.
For a given disk radius R, we are able to ﬁnd 15 or more such combinations for which, Υ is calculated and the largest value is then plotted in Fig. 2
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own description of how Fig. 2 was produced, supplementary section II.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the quantum Zeno effect can give a large effective nonlinearity at the single-photon level, and that a multimode analysis with realistically achievable parameters shows a deterministic phase gate between single photons with near-ideal fidelity.
quotes: we have proposed using the quantum Zeno eﬀect to achieve a large eﬀective nonlinearity at the single-photon level.
we have shown that a deterministic phase gate can be implemented between single photons with near-ideal ﬁdelity.
assertions.certainty_reason: The conclusion rests on simulations at chosen parameters; no experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no device measurement; its realism depends on the cited fabrication and Q-factor assumptions.

assertions.value: The authors state that cavity-enhanced schemes with resonant photon-atom coupling need large setups and near-zero-temperature operation, and that post-selection or feed-forward schemes using only linear optics are inherently probabilistic.
quotes: the implementation requires large setups and operation in near-zero-temperature environment, making such systems unsuitable for practical use.
Such schemes, however, are inherently probabilistic and thus their use is hard to justify in large-scale applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: A motivating statement by the authors with citations but no evidence in this paper.
